## Summary

Did 3.2, per-task routing, closing Phase 3. A plan task now carries `route {agent, model, effort}` (TaskRoute in packages/schema, validated strictly because it carries no enum a newer engine could extend, folded onto TaskState, rendered beside the task in plan.md, and dropped by a full-replace plan that omits it exactly as a status is). driver/routing.ts holds the whole rule set: resolveRoute per launch, previewRoutes over the entire queue before run_started. Two rules, D10. RUN OVER TASK — the recorded surface's model/effort, or the driver's own flags, beat the hint, because a run whose second half ran a model its record does not name is two runs wearing one id; the losing hint is stated on the progress stream rather than dropped. NO SILENT FALLBACK — route.agent naming an adapter the run cannot reach, or one that cannot run the run's policy (threshold on codex, no gauge, no nudge), refuses before anything is recorded, however far down the queue the task sits. Nothing new is recorded: the plan carries the hint, session_started carries the tool and model that actually ran, so no handoff or run_started field asserts a route. Three supporting changes: the run's opening progress lines are now buffered and printed only once the run is certain to start (a refusal used to be able to follow "run <id> — ..."); inertOptions grew the model/effort pair, which was a real gap — a pinned model against an adapter that honours none passed silently before; and nextTask is now the head of queuedTasks rather than a second traversal that could disagree with it. The CLI owns the agent map (bin and agent-args reach only the agent that was named, routed adapters take their own defaults, the default adapter is the same instance in both places). Verified end to end against the built CLI on a scratch record: plan.md renders the route, an unreachable agent and a threshold-incompatible route each refuse with zero run_started, and the D9 warning stream names the routed tasks. Suite 1849 green, typecheck clean, ARCHITECTURE and SPEC (State, MCP tools, driver section, Acceptance criteria) updated.

## Next action

Do 4.1: drive one real initiative end to end unattended and publish the numbers — sessions, handoffs by reason, tokens versus the manual baseline, operator minutes. Pick a small real initiative in this repo, run it with the task policy first (it needs no gauge and runs identically on every adapter), and give the run an allow-list carrying this repo's own proof commands, since the protocol floor deliberately excludes npm test and a session that cannot prove a task done stalls. Two things 3.2 leaves ready: the run is now readable after the fact from the progress stream alone, and per-task routing means the proof run can put one task on codex without a second run.
